title: Stop teammates sealing each other in
hypothesis: In dense swarms, a long dragon gets boxed in by teammates' heads from outside its 7x7 view (bot v1 replays: big_empty 104 self and 58 body deaths). Add a rule so a dragon won't enter a small room another teammate's head is already heading into, and keep an exit when teammates are near.

title: Be cautious in unseen corridors
hypothesis: On kelp mazes, dragons enter corridors whose far edges they haven't seen (unseen edges count as open), then newly seen kelp traps them (stronghold: 51 wall and 80 self deaths). Treat unseen edges as risky in the room check, or infer kelp from the map's symmetry once it is known.

title: Scale splitting to pearl supply
hypothesis: Split-at-4 until round 400 loses the round-500 tiebreak on pearl-poor maps (lost Trauma on length: 13 short dragons with longest 6, against one dragon of 9). Make the split size and the round splitting stops depend on the pearl spawns seen and on map area.

title: Use length when capped at 64 dragons
hypothesis: At the 64-dragon cap, long dragons (median length ~20) just wander and get sealed in. Give them a job: sprint to contested pearls, body-block enemy heads, or become the protected king for round 500.

title: Stop avoidable deaths
hypothesis: Classify our own deaths from the latest referee replays (wall, self, body, head-on, no valid action) and fix the biggest avoidable cause at its root, e.g. a pocket check that misses tails that won't move in time.

title: Trade heads by value, using turn order
hypothesis: An enemy head that moves after us and is adjacent to our target tile can choose to hit us. Treat that as a trade offer: accept only when we lose less length than they do (or we remove their longest dragon), otherwise pick a tile no later-moving enemy head can reach.

title: Body-block kills
hypothesis: When an enemy head that moves after us has 1–2 exits, choose a move that puts our body across them, since ramming a body kills only the rammer. Check that our own escape space stays safe.

title: Short local search over nearby heads
hypothesis: Replace one-step move scoring with a depth-2–3 search over our dragon and enemy heads within 4 tiles (enemies moving after us are true replies, earlier ones are fixed), extending while any head is within 2 tiles. Keep p99 CPU under 50M.

title: Territory-aware pearl choice
hypothesis: Score moves by pearls in our Voronoi territory (multi-source BFS from every visible head on the torus; ties go to nobody) instead of the nearest pearl, so dragons stop chasing pearls an enemy reaches first.

title: Remembered countdowns as targets
hypothesis: Keep a per-dragon memory of seen pearl countdowns (they tick down 1 per round) and route idle dragons to tiles whose spawn time matches their arrival time, in their own territory.

title: Adaptive split policy
hypothesis: Make the split threshold and child size depend on map area, visible pearl density and our dragon count (e.g. split at 5 into 3+2 on sparse maps), instead of always splitting 2 off at length 4.

title: Grow a king for round 500
hypothesis: From a round threshold, the locally longest dragon stops splitting and avoids all head-on risk, while nearby teammates stop competing for its pearls. The round-500 tiebreak is the longest single dragon, and top teams only reach 10–23.

title: Feed the king
hypothesis: Late in the game, short teammates next to the king's path deliberately die so the king can eat their dropped pearls (a dead dragon drops a pearl on every second segment).

title: Sprint to win contested pearls and escape pockets
hypothesis: Nobody sprints (under 1% of moves). Allow 2–3 step sprints when they reach a contested pearl first or escape a closing pocket, paying segments only when the gain is worth it.

title: Detect the map's symmetry early
hypothesis: Infer which of the 3 symmetries (x mirror, y mirror, 180° rotation) the map uses from walls and pearl countdowns seen so far. Use it to predict where the enemy started and where unseen walls are.

title: Parent-child sonar after a split
hypothesis: Right after a split the child faces away from the parent. Use one authenticated sonar ping (a keyed checksum over round and position) so the two pick different directions or targets.

title: Sonar gradients for enemy sightings
hypothesis: Relay a compact 'enemy swarm at (x,y), round r' message outward only, with a hop count, so dragons far away can avoid or reinforce. Always authenticate.

title: No heavy work on a dragon's first turn
hypothesis: Measure first-turn CPU for split children on crowded maps and move any setup work to later turns. MIT teams lost as top seed to first-turn overruns.

title: Anti-oscillation
hypothesis: Penalise moving back to tiles visited in the last few turns when nothing changed, so idle dragons explore instead of pacing.
